profile.entities: Pajson Agro India Ltd (Parent); Pajson Group (Sourcing Arm)
profile.subseg: B2B Institutional Kernels; B2C Branded Dry Fruits (Royal Mewa)
profile.themes: Capacity Expansion; Import Substitution; Brand Premiumization; Forex Volatility

bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds (INR 74.45 Cr) primarily deployed for capex (INR 57 Cr allocated) and general corporate purposes (INR 10.42 Cr); Working capital funded via bank limits (~8.15% interest rate); No dividend announced, focus on reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Forex volatility (100% raw material import exposure); Geopolitical tensions affecting shipping costs (though routes currently clear); Raw material price fluctuations (West African crop dependency); Execution risk on new plant commissioning (Nov-Dec FY27 trial).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on operational moat (farm-gate sourcing) and tech upgrades; Pragmatic on margin pressures (temporary forex impact); Aggressive on capacity expansion timeline; Cautious on brand spend (margin-accretive growth only).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Tech upgrade in Nov-2023 (shelling/color sorters) drove kernel recovery ratio improvement and reduced contamination, fundamentally altering cost structure before IPO; 70:30 whole-to-broken ratio achieved is a key profitability lever; India's 30-35% global consumption share creates a massive import-substitution runway.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: B2B Institutional (bulk kernels for confectioners) remains volume driver; B2C 'Royal Mewa' brand grew 6.5x YoY, targeting Gen Z/millennials via online/offline channels; Export contribution nil in FY26 (vs some in FY25), focused on domestic consumption.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising branded snack demand among Indian millennials/Gen Z seeking healthy options | Pajson Agro India Ltd | beneficiary | High | Royal Mewa brand grew 6.5x; shifting mix from low-margin B2B to higher-margin B2C insulates against commodity cycles. |
| Forex depreciation increasing import costs for all cashew processors | Unorganized Cashew Processors | loser | Med | Lack hedging mechanisms and scale to absorb FX shocks or invest in automation, leading to margin erosion vs organized players like Pajson. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: H2 margin compression (18% -> 11%) driven by: 1) 10.5% INR depreciation vs USD (procurement cost); 2) One-off IPO listing expenses; 3) Late-year RCN price spikes. Mitigation via hedging initiation and partial price pass-through.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~20% from existing capacity in FY27 + new plant contribution (15% util in FY27, 65-70% in FY28); Margin: Steady-state EBITDA 15-16% (FY27 guided); Order Inflow: High repeat demand, expanding distributor base; Capex: INR 76 Cr total for new Vizianagaram plant (INR 39.5 Cr POs issued as of Mar '26).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No multi-year contracts; institutional clients provide 1-3 month visibility; 78% revenue from repeat customers indicating strong demand visibility rather than contractual backlog.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Greenfield expansion to 70k MT by FY30 (from 18k MT); Entry into quick commerce (Blinkit/Zepto); Potential re-entry into export markets (US/EU) post-FY28 once new capacity stabilizes; Backward integration into Indian sourcing to mitigate import risks.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Pajson Agro delivered strong top-line growth (37% YoY) driven by tech-led yield improvements and distribution expansion, though H2 margins compressed to ~11% due to forex headwinds and IPO costs. The strategic pivot lies in the upcoming 35k MT greenfield facility (FY27-28) targeting automated efficiency and a high-margin B2C brand push, aiming to normalize EBITDA at 15-16% despite global sourcing risks.
